cells.tense: You're seeing clearly right now, and the seeing isn't aimed at anything yet.
cells.verb: seeing before there's anything in particular to see
cells.place: oriented toward the light you already steer by
cells.ask: One option open to you: let this clarity stay unproven a while — shine because it's what you are, not to show anyone — and let what comes back be the light answering from other people.
cells.core: You're seeing clearly right now, and the seeing isn't aimed at anything yet. Nothing's been sorted, nothing's been judged — it's the clean look before any of that starts. And you're pointed at what you actually want, not at what you think you should want. That combination is rare and it's working.
cells.sheetLine: You're seeing clearly, and it isn't aimed at anything yet.

cells.tense: You'll have seen it before it happens.
cells.place: steering by a star you've already arrived at
cells.ask: One option open to you: let a moment arrive without knowing what it means first — open, unarmed, fresh — and let the seeing come back to what's actually here instead of what's coming.
cells.core: You'll have seen it before it happens. The clarity is running ahead of the moment — you're already reading what's next, already sure how it lands, already bracing. And that's costing you the light you're steering by, because a star you've already arrived at isn't guiding anything. Knowing ahead of time has replaced being here in time.
cells.sheetLine: You've already read what's next, and it hasn't happened yet.

cells.tense: You saw it once, back there, and you're still standing where it happened.
cells.verb: turning away from the first look
cells.place: far from the light you know how to want
cells.ask: One option open to you: put your hands on one thing you've been meaning to finish — a form, a direction, something with edges — and let choosing it from clarity, not from should, bring the wanting back.
cells.core: You saw it once, back there, and you're still standing where it happened. The clear look came and something about it didn't go well, so the looking stopped — and now you're not aimed anywhere. It isn't that the light went out. It's that you stopped turning toward it.
cells.sheetLine: The seeing came once, and you stopped looking.

cells.tense: You're already seeing clearly, right now, and describing it as something else.
cells.place: oriented by a light you call something ordinary
cells.ask: One option open to you: take one thing you already see plainly and say, out loud, "I saw this" — and let claiming it be shining because it's what you are, not to prove anything.
cells.core: You're already seeing clearly, right now, and describing it as something else. The first look has been arriving — in what you notice, in what you refuse to unsee, in the pull toward what you actually want — and you keep giving the credit to circumstance, to other people, to the obvious. The clarity is running. The claim on it isn't.
cells.sheetLine: You're already seeing it. You just haven't said so.
